rules.ACT-S001: A hook runs a command on a session-start event, so opening a session runs it before anybody has read anything.
rules.ACT-S002: An HTTP hook posts the event's JSON input to a host that is not the loopback interface.
rules.ACT-S003: A hook runs a script inside this repository, so whoever can land a commit decides what it runs.
rules.ACT-S004: A hook runs a path outside this tree, which the repository's own history does not record.
rules.ACT-S005: A hook names a script that is not in the tree, so creating that file later needs no change to any settings file.
rules.ACT-S006: A settings key that executes a command is set from a repository file.
rules.ACT-S007: The permission mode declared in a repository file removes a confirmation the vendor's own default requires.
rules.ACT-S008: An additional directory grants file access outside this repository.
rules.ACT-S009: An allow rule pre-approves shell execution without narrowing it to a command.
rules.ACT-S010: The repository approves its own MCP servers.
rules.ACT-S011: An MCP server is launched through npx or uvx with no version pinned, so it fetches whatever the registry serves at that moment.
rules.ACT-S012: An MCP server is reached over a remote transport, so tool calls and their arguments leave this machine.
rules.ACT-S013: This repository adds a sandbox network domain the managed policy does not list.
rules.ACT-S014: This repository excludes a command from the sandbox that the managed policy does not exclude.
rules.ACT-S015: The sandbox is switched off, or a command may retry outside it.
rules.ACT-S016: A VS Code task runs when the folder is opened, so cloning the repository and opening it runs the task.
rules.ACT-S017: A dev container lifecycle command runs on the host machine, outside the container, before any container exists.
rules.ACT-S018: A dev container mounts a directory that holds credentials, so what is inside it is available to whatever runs in the container.
rules.ACT-S019: A dev container is configured with privileged mode, an added capability or a security option, each of which widens what the container may do.
rules.ACT-S020: A dev container Feature is named without a version, so the build fetches whatever the registry serves at the moment it runs.
rules.ACT-S021: A Codex hook runs a command on a session event, so starting a session runs it before anybody has read anything.
rules.ACT-S022: A Codex setting turns off the sandbox or stops the agent asking before it acts.
rules.ACT-S023: A Codex MCP server is launched without a pinned version, so it resolves to whatever the registry serves when the server starts.
rules.ACT-S024: A Cursor hook runs a command when a session starts or a workspace opens, so it runs before anybody has read the repository.
rules.ACT-S025: A Cursor MCP server is launched without a pinned version, so it resolves to whatever the registry serves when the server starts.
rules.ACT-S026: A Gemini CLI MCP server is launched without a pinned version, so it resolves to whatever the registry serves when the server starts.
rules.ACT-S027: A Gemini CLI MCP server is marked trusted in the configuration, which bypasses every tool call confirmation for that server.
rules.ACT-S028: An instructions file imports a path that resolves outside the repository, so what it loads is not in the tree that was reviewed.
rules.ACT-S029: An instructions file contains a literal command that downloads a remote script and pipes it into an interpreter.
rules.ACT-S030: An instructions file names a script by path, so what runs is whatever is at that path when it is read.
rules.ACT-S031: A Gemini CLI settings file in this repository sets an approval mode that auto-approves edit tools, and a project file overrides the user's.
rules.ACT-S032: A hook invokes an MCP tool on a session-start event, so opening a session makes the tool call before anybody has read anything.

ui.surface.not_read: Seen and not read by this release: {count}
ui.surface.nothing_fired: no rule fired. That is not safety: a repository can be badly configured for a reason no rule names (published limit 9).
ui.surface.vendor_unresolved: {count} capability/capabilities here could not be resolved; they are listed under "Could not be resolved" below, with the cause.
ui.verify.advisory_legend: [{mark}] a known limit on what this verification can claim, not something that went wrong. It does not change the result.
ui.verify.extends: Checking that this package is an append-only extension of {older}
ui.watch.complete: complete: every observed call has a recorded result and the session ended
ui.watch.explain.baseline: First observation. There was nothing to compare against, so a baseline is written and nothing is reported as changed.
ui.watch.explain.content_drift: Bytes moved. Only the changed artifacts are re-analysed, and only the evidence bound to the digests that are gone is superseded.
ui.watch.explain.incomplete: The listing could not be read in full, so no baseline is written. The stored state is left exactly as it was.
ui.watch.explain.source_drift: The revision moved and every digest is the same. A re-tag or a mirror re-upload: recorded, and not the alarm a weight file changing is.
ui.watch.explain.unchanged: Same listing, same digests. Nothing is re-analysed and nothing new is written.
